exchanges.speaker: Pilot
exchanges.text: Hong Kong Radar, Cathay two five one, level Flight Level three fife zero, overhead SIKOU.
exchanges.meaning: En-route initial check-in: pilot reports flight level and position to the new control sector.

exchanges.speaker: ATC
exchanges.text: Cathay two five one, Hong Kong Radar, contact Guangzhou Control wun tree two day-see-mal fife, CPDLC logoff.
exchanges.meaning: Instruction to establish two-way comms on the new frequency and log off datalink authority.

exchanges.speaker: Pilot
exchanges.text: Contact Guangzhou Control wun tree two day-see-mal fife, CPDLC logoff, Cathay two five one.
exchanges.meaning: Correct readback of the frequency transfer instruction.

exchanges.speaker: Pilot
exchanges.text: Hong Kong Radar, Cathay two five one, unable contact Guangzhou on wun tree two day-see-mal fife, frequency silent.
exchanges.meaning: Lost-comms report: the assigned frequency is dead after no response.

exchanges.speaker: ATC
exchanges.text: Cathay two five one, correction, contact Guangzhou Control on secondary wun two fow-er day-see-mal zero fife, monitor guard wun two wun day-see-mal fife.
exchanges.meaning: Corrected secondary frequency assignment plus an order to maintain a listening watch on the guard frequency.

exchanges.speaker: Pilot
exchanges.text: Contact Guangzhou Control wun two fow-er day-see-mal zero fife, monitor guard wun two wun day-see-mal fife, Cathay two five one.
exchanges.meaning: Readback of the corrected frequency and the guard-monitoring instruction.

vocabulary.definition: Instruction to switch frequency and establish active two-way communication.
Instruction to switch frequency and maintain a listening watch without transmitting.
The international emergency distress frequency monitored in cruise as an airliner's lifeline.
Controller-Pilot Data Link Communications: electronic text messaging that transfers ATC authority between ground systems.
Report that an assigned frequency has no response, triggering return to the previous frequency.
Flight Information Region: a defined airspace volume managed by one control authority.
No Radio: an aircraft unable to communicate by radio.

quiz.question: What is the primary difference between the instructions "Contact [facility] [frequency]" and "Monitor [facility] [frequency]"?
options: "Monitor" requires reading back weather reports; "Contact" does not.
"Contact" requires establishing two-way voice communication; "Monitor" requires maintaining a listening watch without transmitting.
"Monitor" is only used for military airspace.
quiz.explanation: Under ICAO Doc 9432, "Contact" instructs the pilot to establish active two-way communications, whereas "Monitor" instructs the pilot to maintain a listening watch on the specified frequency without transmitting.

quiz.question: If a flight crew attempts to establish communication on a newly assigned en-route control frequency and receives no response after repeated calls, what is the correct initial procedure?
options: Verify frequency dialed, check audio panel switches/volume, and return immediately to the previously assigned frequency.
Squawk 7700 immediately and descend to minimum safe altitude.
Turn off transponder and continue on track.
Switch to local approach control frequency without clearance.
quiz.explanation: Standard ICAO lost-comms troubleshooting requires verifying radio selection, checking audio volume/switches, and reverting to the last working frequency to advise the previous controller.

sections.heading: Section 2: Core Learning Content & Vocabulary Table
sections.body:
| Phrase / Command | ICAO Standard Definition | Operational Example |
|---|---|
| Contact [facility] [freq] | Instruction to switch frequency and establish active 2-way comms. | "Contact Guangzhou Control 132.5." |
| Monitor [facility] [freq] | Instruction to switch frequency and listen without transmitting. | "Monitor Guangzhou 132.5." |
| Monitor guard 121.5 | Requirement to maintain listening watch on the emergency distress frequency. | Used during lost comms or long-haul cruising. |
| CPDLC logoff / logon | Disconnecting or establishing datalink with a ground authority. | Transfers electronic ATC text authority. |
| Frequency silent | Report that the assigned frequency has no response. | Triggers return to the previous frequency. |

sections.heading: Section 8: Spaced Repetition Review Drill
sections.body:
- Day 19 Review (+1d): standard 6-part ICAO position report sequence. Any estimated time change of 2 minutes or more requires an immediate update to ATC.
- Day 17 Review (+3d): semicircular rule — Eastbound (000°–179°) = ODD flight levels, Westbound (180°–359°) = EVEN flight levels. RVSM maintains 1,000 ft vertical separation.

sections.heading: Section 9: Fun Aviation Fact — Guard 121.5 & Supersonic Intercepts
sections.body: When an airliner experiences a "NORDO" (No Radio) event because pilots mistuned a frequency or fell asleep, military radar triggers a Quick Reaction Alert (QRA): supersonic fighter jets scramble within minutes, and military controllers broadcast urgent intercept warnings on 121.5 MHz — "Unidentified aircraft cruising over waypoint X, rock your wings immediately or you will be intercepted." That is why monitoring Guard 121.5 is an airliner's ultimate lifeline!
